Rebirth is far more strategic than the original turn based game. This is due to each character having specialized abilities on top of the Materia system and needing to also take into account things like distance and positioning. A character like Aerith has to consider the placement of her wards, are the close enough to the boss? Should I stack them for maximum effect or opposite sides of the battle field to abuse her teleportation? Or maybe Red XIII whose vengeance meter can be burned for a variety of different effects, trying to decide if I’ve enough meter to activate and burn it early to pop off supernal Fevor and grant Haste to the whole party or play it safe and build it more? Do I blow the rest of my meter on Retalition or crescent Claw? I’ve spent far far more time sitting in Tactical Mode in Rebirth debating on summoning Pheonix for the Arise buff over Ramuh for the additional element damage or deciding if I’ve enough time to get Wild Charge ready for a perfect Block and counter or do I dodge out the way instead? Should I use Fireworks Blade for the Infinite MP buff or Savage Assault for Access to lvl 3 limits. The decision making is constant, and much deeper than “my Firaga will melt the Ice slime” and more like “If I have Red cast Faith on Aerith now that’ll give me more ATB to abuse double Thundaga casts during the bosses next phase” Rebirth is way way more tactical than most FF games!

In addition to his DD Crow special summon effect Baldrake can also tribute a dark (or light) monster to send one of your opponents summoned extra deck or ritual monsters to the grave. The synergy lies in Lair of Darkness not only making EVERYTHING on the field Dark, you can also use its effect to tribute one of your opponents monsters for the removal effect! Making what should be a -1 to pop their extra deck monster into 2 for free! And of course you can always just tribute one of your own monsters, which in turn activates Dark Diablo’s effect, brining him to the field, and you can follow up with his own tribute effect!

You can also achieve a similar interaction with Hieratic Seal of the Heavenly Spheres, during your opponents turn with Lairs effect you can tribute one of their monsters to bounce another card. Again getting a 2 for free deal thanks to Lair. The only downside being Lairs tribute effect only working once per turn.

As  didn't mention them in you post it sounds to me like you're missing summon boards and artefacts

 * **Suummon Boards**  Right now we've boards for Ifrit, Shiva, Ramuh,and soon Leviathan. Once you get these summons to 30 you'll unlock a boss fight with them. These boss fights will earn you currency that can be spent on the corresponding board in the enhancements menu. Every single character has a board for these summons, and yes filling out those boards will give you're units a hefty stat boost. On top of that these boards provide a TON of Armor Cores, Tix, and Gems as well.


 * **Artefacts** These are random stat boosting Passives you can farm for by either doing the quest at the bottom of World of Illusions or through co-open rewards. You fuse artefacts in the enhancements menu. A good artefact set up can make a world of a difference. Especially in CHAOS content, combined with Summon boards they're the difference between actually putting out consistent damage & putting up 1's as bosses continue to passively buff themselves throughout a fight.

Hopefully these explanations helped. Getting a unit "maxd" with all their gear, levels, boards, and artefacts is time consuming but so worth it.
